clue.text: Old guide book was hard to get translated

indicators.note: to translate is to turn into another form, so these letters are rendered in a new order

explanation.surface: A hard-to-find old reference book, the speaker remembers, needed translating.
explanation.walkthrough: 'translated' rearranges WASHARD into RADSHAW, placed after B. 'Old guide book' looks like one phrase, but the definition stops at 'guide'. Bradshaw's was the Victorian British railway timetable.
explanation.definitionFit: Bradshaw's Railway Guide was the standard British train timetable of the nineteenth century, a famous historical guide.

clue.text: Farmer organised that woman to bring in first of cows

indicators.note: the pair of words take a letter into their midst, a container signal

parts.note: to run a business is to organise it, so organised gives ran
her is the pronoun pointing at that woman

indicators.note: first of signals picking only the opening letter of the next word

explanation.surface: A farmer arranges for a woman to round up the leading cow.
explanation.walkthrough: 'to bring in' puts C, the first letter of 'cows', between RAN and HER.
explanation.definitionFit: A cattle farmer who runs a large livestock farm in the Americas is called by this title.

clue.text: Fluttering birds make to 2 leave?

indicators.note: fluttering suggests something moving about restlessly, so these letters are shaken into a new order

explanation.surface: Birds flapping their wings seem about to fly off.
explanation.walkthrough: 'Fluttering' rearranges BIRDSMAKE. The '2' as held is a stray character from the newspaper text and plays no part.
explanation.definitionFit: To get off a ship or aircraft is to depart from it, the usual sense of the verb.

clue.text: Prophet identified in whose articles?

indicators.note: identified in says the answer can be found within the letters of the words that follow

explanation.surface: A question asking whose writings a prophet is named in.
explanation.walkthrough: The answer runs across 'wHOSE Articles'.
explanation.definitionFit: Hosea is one of the minor prophets of the Hebrew Bible, with a book bearing his name.

clue.text: National song appropriate for Viennese girl?

explanation.surface: What would suit a girl from Vienna, a city of ballroom dancing?
explanation.walkthrough: The second reading takes the title literally: a Viennese girl called Matilda would naturally be waltzing, Vienna being home of the waltz.
explanation.definitionFit: Australia's unofficial national song is the bush ballad of the swagman; read literally it describes a girl named Matilda dancing in three-four time, apt in Vienna.

clue.text: Advertise band around last in Top 50

indicators.note: around tells us the band wraps itself about the other letters

parts.note: a sash is a band of cloth worn over the shoulder

indicators.note: last in picks the final letter of the following word

parts.note: L is the Roman numeral for fifty

explanation.surface: A band tries to publicise itself after scraping into the charts.
explanation.walkthrough: 'around' puts P (the last letter of 'Top') and L inside SASH. 'band' reads as a pop group but is a sash.
explanation.definitionFit: To splash something is to publicise it prominently, as a newspaper splashes a story across the front page.

clue.text: Drunk's turned up? Serve you right?

parts.note: a sot is a drunkard; the 's stands for 'is', joining the two halves
someone who has turned up has arrived, so is here

explanation.surface: A drunk appears, prompting a smug remark that it serves you right.
explanation.walkthrough: Read 'Drunk's turned up' as 'drunkard is present': SOT + HERE.
explanation.definitionFit: The retort is a childish exclamation of triumph, saying the other person got what they deserved.

clue.text: Not now? Dead right!

parts.note: the late so-and-so is someone who has died

explanation.surface: Someone asks whether it can wait, and is told emphatically yes.
explanation.walkthrough: 'Dead right!' looks like an emphatic agreement but breaks into two pieces.
explanation.definitionFit: Something postponed happens at a subsequent time rather than at this moment.

clue.text: Cut in newspaper exclusive about inflation measure is a sign

indicators.note: about means surrounding, so the shortened word goes round the measure
cut here means docked, the word losing its final letter

parts.note: a scoop is a story one paper gets before its rivals
RPI is the Retail Prices Index, the British measure of inflation

explanation.surface: A newspaper exclusive about inflation figures gets edited down.
explanation.walkthrough: 'Cut' trims SCOOP to SCOO, and 'about' wraps it round RPI. RPI, the Retail Prices Index, is a British measure of inflation.
explanation.definitionFit: Scorpio is one of the twelve signs of the zodiac, the scorpion.

clue.text: Insects heading away from county, in short

indicators.note: heading away means the first letter departs from the word

parts.note: Hants is the short form of Hampshire, an English county

explanation.surface: Insects leaving a county, briefly put.
explanation.walkthrough: HANTS, the abbreviation of Hampshire, a county in southern England, loses its first letter.
explanation.definitionFit: Ants are small social insects living in colonies.

clue.text: Position that receives almost wholly high-class greeting

indicators.note: receives says the first word takes the others inside it

parts.note: a station is a post or position someone occupies

indicators.note: almost means the word stops one letter short of its end

parts.note: all means wholly, as in all alone
U is the crossword label for upper-class usage

explanation.surface: A post that admits a nearly complete upper-class welcome.
explanation.walkthrough: 'almost' cuts ALL to AL, and 'receives' puts AL + U inside STATION.
explanation.definitionFit: A salutation is a formal word or gesture of welcome.

clue.text: Agree to bring in tank mostly for zoo creature?

indicators.note: to bring in means the first word takes the next inside it

parts.note: to chime with something is to agree with it

indicators.note: mostly means the word loses its last letter

parts.note: a Panzer is a German tank

explanation.surface: Consenting to bring in a military vehicle to house an animal.
explanation.walkthrough: 'mostly' trims PANZER to PANZE, and 'to bring in' puts it inside CHIME.
explanation.definitionFit: Chimpanzees are apes commonly kept in zoos; the question mark admits they are not only found there.

clue.text: Recipe suitable to be consumed

parts.note: R is the abbreviation for recipe, from Latin, as on prescriptions
apt means fitting or suitable

explanation.surface: A recipe fit to be eaten.
explanation.walkthrough: Recipe as R is the prescription mark, Latin 'recipe' meaning take.
explanation.definitionFit: Someone wholly absorbed or engrossed in something is consumed by it.

clue.text: Recalled prank involving a South African village

indicators.note: involving means taking in, so the reversed word goes round the letter
recalled here means called back, the word read in reverse

parts.note: a lark is a prank or bit of fun

explanation.surface: A remembered practical joke in a village in South Africa.
explanation.walkthrough: 'Recalled' turns LARK to KRAL, and 'involving' puts A inside it.
explanation.definitionFit: A kraal is a traditional enclosed settlement of huts in southern Africa.

clue.text: Hare found running? (That's hardly this!)

indicators.note: running suggests movement, so these letters are set in motion into a new order

explanation.surface: A hare seen running, which is no surprise at all.
explanation.walkthrough: 'running' rearranges HAREFOUND. The definition is the bracketed comment: a hare caught running is hardly a rare sight.
explanation.definitionFit: Something never known before is unprecedented; a running hare is everyday, so it is hardly that.

clue.text: Gives audition to participant in authentic theatrical event

indicators.note: a participant in something takes part inside it, so one word sits within the other

parts.note: real means genuine or authentic
a casting director hears an actor at an audition

explanation.surface: Someone auditions an actor for a genuine stage production.
explanation.walkthrough: 'participant in' puts HEARS inside REAL.
explanation.definitionFit: A rehearsal is a practice performance of a play before it opens.

clue.text: Very upset with measure of current mining hazard

parts.note: choked is British slang for very upset or emotional
an amp is the unit of electric current

explanation.surface: Distressed by an electrical reading in a dangerous mine.
explanation.walkthrough: 'choked' as 'very upset' is British informal usage.
explanation.definitionFit: Chokedamp is the suffocating gas, mainly carbon dioxide, that builds up in mines.

clue.text: A measure of security involving locks?

definitions.text: A measure of security involving locks?

parts.words: A measure of security involving locks?
parts.note: the locks are not on doors but the locks of hair, and the security a slick product that keeps them in place

explanation.surface: A safety measure that depends on locks.
explanation.walkthrough: Locks suggest doors and security, but here they are tresses of hair kept tidy by a grooming product.
explanation.definitionFit: Hair-oil is a grooming product that holds hair in place, keeping the locks secure.

clue.text: Madden the German and the old Brit, deporting Liberal

parts.note: der is the German masculine definite article

indicators.note: deporting means sending out, so the letter is removed from the word

parts.note: the Angles were an early Germanic people who settled Britain

explanation.surface: The German and an ancient Briton infuriate someone by expelling a Liberal.
explanation.walkthrough: 'deporting' drops L from ANGLE, giving ANGE after DER.
explanation.definitionFit: To derange someone is to drive them mad.

clue.text: Cathedral city denying holy man comfort

indicators.note: denying means refusing entry, so letters are taken out

parts.note: Chester is a cathedral city in Cheshire, England
ST is the abbreviation for saint

explanation.surface: A cathedral city refusing a holy man any comfort.
explanation.walkthrough: CHESTER, a cathedral city in north-west England, loses ST.
explanation.definitionFit: To cheer someone is to comfort or encourage them.

clue.text: Lonely, avoiding Friday at all times

definitions.note: an adverb phrase defining an adjective: an endless thing goes on at all times

indicators.note: avoiding means going without, so letters are removed

parts.note: someone friendless is lonely

explanation.surface: A lonely person who keeps away from Friday, always.
explanation.walkthrough: FRIENDLESS without FRI.
explanation.definitionFit: Something unceasing never stops, so it continues at all times.

clue.text: Stable tree by top of mountain

parts.note: a fir is a coniferous tree

indicators.note: top of in a clue means the first letter of the next word

explanation.surface: A steady tree near a mountain summit.
explanation.definitionFit: Firm means steady or secure, the same sense as stable.

clue.text: Greek heroine having me all but cold

indicators.note: all but means all except the last letter

parts.note: dead and cold are both words for lifeless

explanation.surface: A Greek heroine who leaves the speaker nearly frozen.
explanation.walkthrough: 'all but' trims DEAD to DEA, after ME.
explanation.definitionFit: Medea, the sorceress who helped Jason, is the tragic heroine of Euripides' play.

clue.text: Trio, agitato, embracing a way with slowing down

indicators.note: embracing means holding inside, so the stirred letters go round the rest
agitato is a musical direction meaning agitated, so the letters are stirred up

parts.note: RD is the abbreviation for road, a way
and joins one thing with another

explanation.surface: An agitated trio of musicians loses tempo along the way.
explanation.walkthrough: 'agitato' rearranges TRIO into RITO, and 'embracing' puts A + RD + AND inside it.
explanation.definitionFit: Ritardando is the musical direction for a gradual decrease in tempo.

clue.text: Dissolute type, note, in French city

parts.note: a roue is a debauched, dissolute man

explanation.surface: A rake and a note found in a French city.
explanation.definitionFit: Rouen is a city in Normandy, on the Seine.

clue.text: High-class rock bun cooled around middle of afternoon

indicators.note: around means the shaken letters surround another
to rock is to shake, so these letters are shaken into a new order
middle of picks the central letter of the word

explanation.surface: A posh rock bun left to cool at teatime.
explanation.walkthrough: 'rock' looks like part of 'rock bun' but it is the anagram signal for BUN + COOLED, which goes 'around' R, the middle letter of 'afternoon'.
explanation.definitionFit: Cordon bleu describes first-rate cookery, the highest class of chef.

clue.text: Number of sins not very observed

indicators.note: not here means without, so the letter is dropped

parts.note: there are seven deadly sins

explanation.surface: How many sins there are, not much witnessed.
explanation.walkthrough: SEVEN, the number of deadly sins, without V gives SEEN; the grid as held prints SEER, but this wordplay and definition give SEEN.
explanation.definitionFit: Something witnessed has been looked at, the past participle of the verb to see.

clue.text: Half of play, without difficulty it seems, is to entertain

indicators.note: half of picks the first two of the four letters of the next word

parts.note: doing something with ease is doing it without difficulty

explanation.surface: Half a play performed effortlessly, it appears, is meant to amuse.
explanation.walkthrough: 'Half of' takes PL from 'play'; 'it seems' and 'is to' are link words.
explanation.definitionFit: To please people is to delight or amuse them, as an entertainer does.

clue.text: Record-keeper and researcher, we hear

indicators.note: we hear says the word is to be taken by its sound, not its spelling

parts.note: an analyst studies and researches data

explanation.surface: A keeper of records and a researcher, so people say.
explanation.walkthrough: 'we hear' turns ANALYST, the researcher, into a word sounding the same.
explanation.definitionFit: An annalist writes annals, the year-by-year historical records, so is a chronicler.
